Machine-learning classification and regression on microbiome features

Source: R/mp_ml.R
mp_ml.Rd

Trains a random forest ("rf") or gradient-boosted trees ("xgb") model on the (optionally transformed) feature table of a phyloseq::phyloseq object, using a sample-metadata column as the response. The task is detected automatically from the response type - classification for a factor/character column, regression for a numeric one - and can be forced with task. Out-of-fold predictions from k-fold cross-validation drive the performance metrics; feature importance comes from a model fit on all samples.

Usage

mp_ml(
  object,
  group.by = NULL,
  method = c("rf", "xgb"),
  task = c("auto", "classification", "regression"),
  tax.level = NULL,
  top.n = NULL,
  transform = c("clr", "relative", "none"),
  plot.type = c("importance", "roc", "confusion", "prediction"),
  n.features = 20,
  cv.folds = 5,
  ntree = 500,
  nrounds = 150,
  seed = NULL,
  palette = NULL,
  theme = NULL,
  ...,
  plot.title = NULL,
  plot.subtitle = NULL,
  plot.caption = NULL,
  font.size = getOption("micropubr.font.size", 11),
  interactive = FALSE,
  return.data = FALSE,
  verbose = getOption("micropubr.verbose", FALSE)
)

Arguments

object

A phyloseq::phyloseq object with counts.

group.by

Sample-metadata column used as the response/outcome.

method

Learner: "rf" (randomForest) or "xgb" (xgboost).

task

"auto" (default), "classification" or "regression".

tax.level

Optional rank to agglomerate features to before modelling.

top.n

Optional number of most-abundant features to keep (dimension reduction); NULL keeps them all.

transform

Feature transform applied before modelling: "clr" (centred log-ratio, the default), "relative" or "none".

plot.type

What to draw: "importance" (ranked feature importance, the default), "roc" (ROC curve, two-class classification only), "confusion" (confusion-matrix heatmap, classification) or "prediction" (observed vs predicted scatter, regression).

n.features

Number of top features shown in the importance plot.

cv.folds

Number of cross-validation folds.

ntree

Number of trees for the random forest.

nrounds

Number of boosting rounds for xgboost.

seed

Optional integer seed for reproducible folds/models.

palette

Palette name or colour vector.

theme

A ggplot2 theme; defaults to the active theme (see mp_set_defaults(), otherwise mp_theme_publication()).

...

Additional arguments passed to the primary geom of the chosen plot (e.g. ggplot2::geom_col() for importance).

plot.title, plot.subtitle, plot.caption

Optional labels.

font.size

Base font size.

interactive

If TRUE, return an interactive plotly widget instead of a static ggplot (requires plotly). See mp_alpha().

return.data

If TRUE, return the tidy feature-importance data frame instead of a plot, with the fitted model (attr(., "model")), the cross-validation predictions (attr(., "cv")) and a named list of performance metrics (attr(., "metrics")) attached as attributes.

verbose

Print the method and performance summary.

Value

A ggplot object, a plotly widget when interactive = TRUE, or a data frame when return.data = TRUE.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data(GlobalPatterns, package = "phyloseq")
gp <- phyloseq::tax_glom(GlobalPatterns, "Genus")
# Classification: which genera discriminate sample types?
mp_ml(gp, group.by = "SampleType", method = "rf")
# Two-class ROC curve.
soil_vs_feces <- phyloseq::subset_samples(
  gp, SampleType %in% c("Soil", "Feces"))
mp_ml(soil_vs_feces, group.by = "SampleType", plot.type = "roc")
} # }
